inputs.share_count_basis: 2,505.667m ordinary shares outstanding at 2026-03-31 (FY2025 20-F beneficial-ownership table: 2,357.167m Class A + 148.5m Class C, excluding 23.0m shares reserved for award plans) plus ~41.4m dilutive awards (Q4 2025 diluted less basic weighted average, the only profitable quarter in which the filer shows the increment). 1 ADS = 1 Class A share. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, and the negative early-year flows already charge the funding gap that past equity raises covered -- compounding the count on top would charge the burn twice. EXCLUDED: the 248.45m performance RSUs granted to the CEO in March 2026 (vest only on market-cap and net-profit milestones far above today's price; charged through the SBC path) and ~134.5m ADSs under the 2027/2029/2030 convertible notes (conversion ~US$11/ADS, deep out of the money -- carried as debt at principal instead). Any share issuance after 2026-03-31 is NOT captured: no later share count is in the filings on hand.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 20-F consolidated cash flow statement, 'Share-based compensation expenses' RMB1,790.7m (ties to the non-GAAP reconciliation). No cash taxes on net-share settlement appear in financing activities (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 every year).
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in RMB (CNY); NYSE ADS quoted in USD; 1 ADS = 1 Class A ordinary share. USD/CNY 6.6712 (Yahoo USDCNY=X, 2026-11-15T03:30Z), so model->quote fx_rate = 1/6.6712 = 0.149898. Parity check against the Hong Kong listing: 9866.HK HK$23.32 (2026-11-13 close) / 7.8455 HKD per USD = US$2.97 versus the NYSE close in current_price, a 2.5% gap consistent with the HK close preceding the US session -- confirms the 1:1 ADS ratio and the rate direction. refresh_price.py does not move fx_rate; re-derive it on any refresh.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 11.5%, built in CNY because the flows are CNY: China 10-year government yield ~1.9% + ~5.7% China equity risk premium x ~1.7 beta (high-volatility EV maker) = ~11.6% cost of equity; debt is a small share of capital (convertibles and bank loans against a larger cash balance), so WACC is set at ~cost of equity, 11.5%. This is roughly 13.5% in USD terms at a ~2pp rate differential. The SAME rate is used in all three scenarios: price-war, supplier-terms, VIE/delisting and multi-brand execution risk are charged in the scenario flows and the 30% bear weight, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B) for operating leases: US GAAP operating lease cost (RMB2.2bn ROU amortisation plus interest in 2025) already sits inside operating expenses and therefore inside the EBITDA margin path; operating lease liabilities (RMB11.9bn at 2026-03-31) are EXCLUDED from net debt. Finance leases are treated as debt: an ESTIMATED RMB4.8bn present value (undiscounted obligations RMB7,203m per the FY2025 20-F contractual-obligations table, RMB5,250m of it beyond five years, discounted at ~4.5%; the lease-balance table did not survive text extraction) is deducted in equity_bridge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated. Redeemable non-controlling interests (NIO China minority investors ~8% and the Shenji chip-subsidiary investors) are deducted once in equity_bridge at their US GAAP carrying/redemption value, RMB10,222.7m at 2026-06-30. Ordinary NCI is immaterial (-RMB20m).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, with the non-US adaptations (CNY flows / USD quote, leases, NCI, matching-asset rule). Routed as an operating company; NIO is not a lender, REIT or holdco. FRESH BUILD -- no prior DCF. | FY0 OWNER FCF: reported FCF -RMB3,073m (OCF 2,993 - capex 6,065) less SBC 1,791 less interest income 762 = -RMB5,625m. FY2025 OCF was flattered by an RMB18.3bn increase in trade and notes payable (partly offset by an RMB8.4bn build in receivables from related parties, chiefly the Battery Asset Company, and RMB3.1bn of inventory); operating cash flow before working capital was -RMB2.8bn. | CASH DEFINITION: cash = cash and equivalents 8,827.5 + short-term investments 22,938.2 at 2026-03-31. Restricted cash of RMB16,390.9m is EXCLUDED: it is collateral for bank acceptance notes inside the RMB54.0bn trade and notes payable, i.e. it is supplier float, not distributable cash. The company's own 'RMB48.2bn cash' headline includes it. | DEBT: short-term borrowings 5,549.0 + current portion of long-term borrowings 736.4 + long-term borrowings 8,389.5 (includes ~US$1.15bn of 2029/2030 convertible notes at principal; holders can put them in October 2027 and October 2028). | PARTIAL LATER DATA: the only Q2 2026 filing on hand is the HKEX US GAAP/IFRS reconciliation (H1 2026 loss from operations -RMB656m, net loss -RMB860m, redeemable NCI RMB10,223m, long-term borrowings RMB8,551m); it carries no cash balance or share count, so net cash and shares stay at 2026-03-31. Q2 revenue (~RMB32.1bn) and deliveries (107,658) are from the Analysis JSON and both came in BELOW the Q1 guidance range (110-115k vehicles, RMB32.8-34.4bn). | BATTERY ASSET COMPANY: NIO holds ~16.5% and does not consolidate it; no BaaS battery assets or subscription cash flows are in these flows. The stake sits in long-term investments (added at book in the bridge) and the equity-method losses (RMB1,092m share of investee losses in 2025) are outside EBITDA -- one side each, per the matching-asset rule. NIO's payment guarantee to the Battery Asset Company and the RMB16.4bn receivable from related parties are unpriced exposures. | BUYBACKS: none; the flat share count is a modelling convention the company is not funding -- it has been a serial net issuer (RMB11.9bn of ordinary shares issued in 2025, RMB21.0bn in 2023). | BAND: SBC is small (1.5-2% of revenue) so the house/street band is narrow relative to the scenario spread.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: base-case average forward revenue growth for years 2-10; equity CAGR is unusable (book equity fell from RMB27.2bn in FY2020 to RMB4.2bn in FY2025 despite ~RMB33bn of ordinary-share issuance in 2023 and 2025)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-31% 5yr, -44% 3yr) diverges from revenue CAGR (+40% 5yr, +21% 3yr) by far more than 30pp: revenue growth has been bought with losses funded by new equity. EPS and owner FCF were negative in every year, so no CAGR exists for either.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income), RMB m: FY2020 +469; FY2021 -4,034; FY2022 -14,493; FY2023 -20,301; FY2024 -19,774; FY2025 -5,625. Cumulative FY2021-FY2025 owner cash burn ~RMB64bn. Diluted share count rose from ~1,527m (FY2020) to ~2,547m, +67%.

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 (FY2026) is three-quarters known: Q1 RMB25.5bn + Q2 ~RMB32.1bn + Q3 guided 108-111k deliveries + a Q4 tracking below the 40k/month target = ~RMB122bn, +39%. FY2027 +15% as ONVO/FIREFLY annualise; FY2028 +6% because the NEV purchase-tax exemption (halved from 2026) ends after 2027 and pulls demand forward; then a fade to 3%. Management's 40-50% volume-growth ambition is NOT underwritten.
base.margin_rationale: Adjusted EBITDA margin is before SBC and after operating lease cost. FY2026 6.8% = GAAP operating margin ~-0.8% (H1 2026 actual -1.1%) + SBC 1.6% + D&A 6.0%. Ramps to 10.5%, i.e. a ~4.5% GAAP operating margin at maturity -- vehicle margin held near 18-19% with R&D and SG&A falling from ~21% of revenue to ~15% on scale. That is BYD/Li Auto-at-peak territory, not premium-European.
base.tax_rationale: Cash taxes were RMB144m in 2025; accumulated deficit ~RMB129bn, though PRC losses expire after 5 years (10 for high-tech enterprises). The shelter is ramped away to a 20% rate (blend of the 15% HNTE and 25% statutory rates) by year 8 and is not perpetuated.
base.wc_rationale: Payables-funded model: FY2025 working capital released ~RMB5.8bn on RMB21.8bn of revenue growth (27%). Only 10% is carried forward because trade and notes payable already run ~200 days of cost of sales and Chinese automakers have pledged 60-day supplier terms.

scenario_narratives.base: The FY2025-26 inflection holds but does not extend in a straight line. The core NIO brand keeps vehicle margin near 18-19% through the memory-chip and battery-material cost inflation management flagged for H2 2026; ONVO and FIREFLY add volume at lower ASPs rather than transforming the mix. Revenue lands ~RMB122bn in FY2026 and compounds at high single digits to ~RMB220bn by FY2035, well short of management's 40-50% volume ambition. R&D and SG&A fall from ~21% of revenue to ~15% on scale and the in-house chip/OS cost-downs, taking the GAAP operating margin from about -1% to ~4.5%. Supplier float still grows with revenue but at a third of the FY2025 rate. Capex stays near 5% of revenue as the swap network densifies. The company does not need another large rescue raise, but the valuation gives it no credit for buybacks either.
scenario_narratives.bull: The multi-brand platform works: ONVO becomes a genuine Model Y-class volume line and FIREFLY scales in compact and export markets without cannibalising the premium brand, taking revenue past RMB330bn (roughly 1.2m vehicles) by FY2035. The swap network turns from a cost centre into a moat that supports pricing while rivals discount, the NX9031 chip and in-house stack deliver the promised bill-of-materials savings, and opex leverage lifts the GAAP operating margin to ~6.8% -- a premium-automaker level no Chinese EV pure-play has sustained. This needs volume, margin and the price war easing to go right together, which is why it carries the smallest weight.
scenario_narratives.bear: The inflection proves to be a peak. After the NEV purchase-tax exemption was halved in 2026, demand is pulled forward and then stalls; the China price war plus RMB14,000+ per-vehicle input-cost inflation push vehicle margin back toward the low teens, ONVO/FIREFLY volumes disappoint against the fixed cost of three brands and 3,700+ swap stations, and revenue falls in FY2027-28. The GAAP operating margin never gets above roughly breakeven, so owner FCF stays negative to marginal and the terminal value is at or near the zero floor -- the operating business is worth little and the equity is an option on refinancing. The flows here do NOT include the harsher tail in which suppliers enforce 60-day terms: unwinding RMB54bn of payables toward that level would absorb the unrestricted cash, force the 2027-28 convertible puts and redeemable-NCI redemptions into a distressed raise, and take the equity toward zero.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 30% (double the house default): net losses every year since IPO, a going-concern/liquidity assessment in the FY2025 20-F, ~200 days of supplier payables, convertible puts in 2027-28 and a Q2 2026 that already missed its own delivery and revenue guidance. Base 45%: four quarters of 18-19% vehicle margin and three quarters of non-GAAP operating profit are real evidence, but not yet a full cycle. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs ONVO and FIREFLY volume, premium-level margins and an easing price war all at once.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A turnaround in progress valued on normalised, not extrapolated, cash flows: neither the RMB64bn of owner cash burned over FY2021-25 nor the last four quarters of margin recovery is run forward in a straight line. Value rests on whether a ~RMB120bn-revenue automaker can hold an 18-19% vehicle margin and take operating costs from ~21% to ~15% of revenue. The reported RMB48bn cash pile is mostly spoken for -- a third is restricted collateral for supplier notes, and debt, finance leases and redeemable minority interests absorb most of the rest -- so the equity is essentially a claim on future operating cash flow with a wide distribution of outcomes.
key_risks_to_valuation: Working capital: RMB54bn of trade and notes payable (~200 days of cost of sales) funds the business; enforcement of 60-day supplier terms would consume the unrestricted cash and is not in any scenario's flows

Dilution outside the model: the share count is held flat, but NIO has issued equity in most years, the CEO holds 248m performance RSUs (~10% of the count), and convertibles are puttable in October 2027 and October 2028
Balance-sheet vintage: net cash and shares are as of 2026-03-31; the Q2 2026 balance sheet and any later issuance are not in the filings on hand, and the finance-lease deduction is an estimate
Price war and input costs: every 1pp of vehicle margin is ~RMB1.1bn of operating profit at the FY2026 run-rate, against a base-case terminal operating margin of only ~4.5%
ONVO/FIREFLY are 1-2 years old; the base case assumes they add volume without earning premium-brand margins, the bull case assumes they do
FX and structure: CNY flows against a USD quote (the rate has moved from ~7.19 to ~6.67 over the 52-week range), VIE structure, US delisting/outbound-investment policy
Battery Asset Company: NIO owns ~16.5%, guarantees user payments to it and carries RMB16.4bn of related-party receivables; none of that exposure is priced beyond book value of the stake
